title: Secondary Physics Scheme of Work: Mechanics and Energy
subject: science
overview: This guide covers the Mechanics and energy unit (Term 2): phys-kinematics, phys-forces, phys-energy.
Work through the key ideas first, follow the revision plan day by day, watch out for the traps, and try the questions together at home.

keyIdeas.explanation: The energy transferred when a force moves its object, calculated as force times distance in the force's direction, measured in joules.
How fast work is done, calculated as work divided by time, measured in watts: the same 200 J in 2 s is 100 W, in 10 s only 20 W.
What work transfers between stores and forms - it is never created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.
The energy a raised mass stores because of its height, calculated as mass times g times height: 2 kg at 5 m stores 98 J.

revisionPlan.focus: Practice set for phys-energy: A moving car brakes to a stop. What happens to its kinetic energy?
Practice set for phys-energy: State the equation linking work done, force and distance.

traps.misconception: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped.
traps.watchFor: Flat reads as "nothing is happening", so the line feels like zero movement. A flat v-t line means constant velocity: the object keeps moving at the same speed. In class, sketch a line flat at 10 m/s and ask how far the object travels in 5 seconds: the area under the flat line is 10 times 5, which is 50 metres - a stopped object travels nowhere.

traps.misconception: The same push gives the same pressure whether you stand flat or on tiptoes.
traps.watchFor: The push feels the same, so the effect on the ground feels like it should be the same. Pressure is force over area: tiptoes spread the same force over a smaller area, so the pressure is higher. In class, keep the force fixed at 200 N and shrink only the area: 0.5 square metres gives 400 Pa, while 0.05 square metres gives 4000 Pa - the push never changed, only its spread.

traps.misconception: Energy gets used up when work is done.
traps.watchFor: The car runs out of petrol and stops, so the energy feels destroyed. Energy is never used up: it changes form, like chemical energy becoming kinetic energy plus heat. In class, follow the falling mass: 98 J of GPE at the top becomes 98 J of KE at the bottom - the form changed, the total did not.

parentQuestions.question: A moving car brakes to a stop. What happens to its kinetic energy?
parentQuestions.answer: It changes into heat and sound; the total energy stays the same.

parentQuestions.question: Which statement about energy is correct?
parentQuestions.answer: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes form.
